notes: 0.1.0a6 is a publication-recovery release. It carries the 0.1.0a5 runtime unchanged after v0.1.0a5 was aborted by publication readiness before the first upload. ADR 0080 records why recovery moved to 0.1.0a6 and Execution Semantics moved intact to 0.1.0a7.

0.1.0a4 was partially published on 2026-09-08. Workflow run 34285830444 uploaded agnara-0.1.0a4-py3-none-any.whl (HTTP 200) and was rejected on agnara_a2a-0.1.0a4-py3-none-any.whl with HTTP 400 'Non-user identities cannot create new projects'. Twine uploads wheels before sdists and stops on the first failure, so the agnara 0.1.0a4 sdist and all twelve sibling artifacts were never uploaded, post-release verification never ran, and no GitHub Release was created. v0.1.0a4 remains historical and unmodified.

The gate that was missing is now explicit. publication-prerequisites re-derives PUBLISH READY from the repository on every run, and pypi-trusted-publishers is a manual gate the tooling can never satisfy. docs/releases/publication.json is the reviewed record of the external registry configuration; it is UNVERIFIED until the owner reads the tuples back from PyPI.
Status is recomputed by scripts/check_release_readiness.py; automated outcomes are never trusted from this file.

gates.title: Every PyPI Trusted Publisher is confirmed for this exact target
gates.detail: Only the repository owner can read a Trusted Publisher tuple back from PyPI. No check running here can observe it, and 0.1.0a4 shipped on the assumption that it had been done. Confirmation is recorded per project in docs/releases/publication.json and must name the target it was made for; the automated publication-prerequisites gate and release.yml both refuse while any project is UNVERIFIED. Readback of the public index at 2026-09-08 from this commit: agnara exists and does not carry 0.1.0a5; agnara-a2a, agnara-cli, agnara-events, agnara-http, agnara-mcp and agnara-telemetry return 404. A 404 does not prove a pending publisher is absent, and it does not prove one is present. The owner must also check https://pypi.org/manage/projects/ for a project created under a misspelled name and remove it and its publisher rather than renaming anything here. No recommendation is possible: this gate is a fact the owner has to observe.
